chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub al-Kulayni narrated, saying: Ali ibn Ibraheem ibn Hashim narrated from his father from Hannan ibn Sadeer from Ma'roof ibn Kharrabooth from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that he said:

"We are like the stars of the sky; whenever a star sets, another rises. But when you point with your fingers and tilt your eyebrows (in confusion), Allah will hide your star from you. Then the children of Abdul Muttalib will become equal, so that one cannot be distinguished from another. When your star rises again, praise your Lord."
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the hadith comparing the Imams to stars in the sky?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Baqir (AS) employs the celestial metaphor of stars to illustrate the continuous, unbroken line of Imamate within the progeny of Abdul Muttalib, ensuring perpetual divine guidance. The phrase 'until you point with your fingers and squint with your eyebrows' signifies a period of confusion or the Great Occultation where the specific Imam becomes less distinct to the general populace, yet the lineage remains intact. The narration concludes with a eschatological promise: once the awaited Imam (the 'star') emerges from his concealment, the community is commanded to express gratitude to God for the restoration of clear, visible guidance.
